names.official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

summary: São Tomé and Príncipe exempts citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries from visas under Law 5/2015, and the UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens 15 days visa-free; other nationalities apply online for an eVisa before arrival.

AO.notes: Visa-free: Law 5/2015 (article 25(1)(e) of the Foreigners Act) exempts citizens of the EU, the United States, Canada and the CPLP member states from visas. The law sets no length of stay. For a longer stay, apply for the eVisa before travelling or ask the Migration and Border Service for an extension.

source.name: Serviço de Migração e Fronteiras — Law 5/2015 amending the Foreigners Act (Diário da República no. 146, 30 November 2015)

fee.notes: Not a published visa fee. The Migration and Border Service's e-visa portal does not show one and says payment is made at the border. The FCDO says British visitors must pay a €20 entry fee on arrival, payable in euros, US dollars or local currency. The SMF's own FAQ gives the temporary tourist visa fee as 490,000 STD, set by a Council of Ministers deliberation of 10 February 2011.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted and there are only a small number of ATMs, with cash available from the main bank in the capital. Canada says cards can be used only at major international hotels, that foreign bank cards cannot be used to withdraw money from ATMs, and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and Central African CFA francs.

safety.text: Canada advises taking normal security precautions in São Tomé and Príncipe. It says petty crime such as pickpocketing and bag-snatching occurs, particularly in markets, on beaches and on busy streets near hotels, and that violent crime is rare but does occur.

tips.text: The UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens a visa-free stay of 15 days, and the exemption law sets no other length. For a longer stay, apply for the eVisa before travelling or ask the Migration and Border Service for an extension before your permitted stay ends.

The UK FCDO says cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few, and Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used to withdraw money from ATMs and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and CFA francs.

Canada's travel advice says malaria is a risk in São Tomé and Príncipe and that antimalarial medication is recommended for most travellers — see a health professional before you go and use insect repellent.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries are exempt from visas under Law 5/2015. The UK government says British visitors need no visa for up to 15 days, and the US and Canadian governments give their citizens the same 15 days; the law itself sets no length of stay. No official source we could read covers Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland. Everyone else — and anyone staying longer — applies online for an eVisa on the Migration and Border Service (SMF) e-visa portal before arrival.

faq.question: How can I stay longer than 15 days?
faq.answer: Apply for the eVisa before travelling, or ask the Migration and Border Service in São Tomé for an extension: under Law 5/2008 (article 43), visitors admitted without a visa can be given up to 30 days more, renewable once for the same period.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The UK government says you need a yellow fever certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

faq.question: What money should I bring to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few; Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used at ATMs and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and Central African CFA francs.
